football_evidence.assessment: No material disagreement: EdgeDesk and the line are within 0.9 points.
supporting: In his last two games (Oregon and Washington), Colandrea averaged 5.1 yards per attempt, against 7.6 in his six games before that.

When Illinois has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Illinois’ offense is stopped at or behind the line on 13.3% of its runs, and Nebraska’s defense stops 19.1% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.5%).
contradicting: When Illinois has the ball (third down): Illinois’ offense converts 42.2% of its third downs, and Nebraska’s defense allows opponents to convert 17.0% of their third downs (FBS average 39.6%).
When Illinois has the ball (the red zone): Illinois’ offense succeeds on 43.0% of its red-zone plays, and Nebraska’s defense allows success on 27.3% of opponent red-zone plays (FBS average 43.5%).

When Illinois has the ball (big plays on the ground): Illinois’ offense turns 6.1% of its runs into explosive gains, and Nebraska’s defense gives up explosive gains on 3.2% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).

When Nebraska has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Nebraska’s offense has allowed a sack on 3.8% of its dropbacks, and Illinois’ defense sacks the quarterback on 3.6% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).
quarterbacks: Katin Houser has completed 140 of 219 passes (63.9%) for 1,663 yards, 7.6 yards per attempt, 13 touchdowns and 5 interceptions in seven games for Illinois, and has been sacked on 6 of 225 dropbacks.
Michael Clayton II has completed 18 of 27 passes (66.7%) for 177 yards, 6.6 yards per attempt, 4 touchdowns and no interceptions in two games for Illinois, and has been sacked on 2 of 29 dropbacks.

Anthony Colandrea has completed 160 of 267 passes (59.9%) for 1,837 yards, 6.9 yards per attempt, 15 touchdowns and 7 interceptions in eight games for Nebraska, and has been sacked on 15 of 282 dropbacks.
